title: Characterization of Dilute Mn Implantation in Bi2Se3 Films via 4D-STEM and EELS
content: Advanced electron microscopy techniques, such as in-situ electron energy loss spectroscopy (EELS) and 4D-Scanning Transmission Electron Microscopy (4D-STEM), have become indispensable for investigating the atomic-scale effects of dopants in functional materials. These methods are particularly crucial for studying doped topological insulators, where the precise location and structural impact of dopant ions are critical for tuning electronic properties. In this work, we leverage low-dose, multiframe EELS and multislice ptychography to study Mn-doped Bi2Se3 thin films, a promising platform for realizing the quantum anomalous Hall effect (QAHE). By combining these techniques with pixelated cameras and advanced signal-averaging approaches, we have been able to overcome the significant challenges of characterizing the subtle structural and electronic effects of low dopant concentrations.
